newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: PRESS DIGEST - Sri Lankan Newspapers - July 23.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Sri Lankan Newspapers - July 23.

text.p: Following is a summary of major Sri Lankan political and business stories prepared for Reuters by NewsWatch, Colombo Tel/Fax: 94-1-735182 Internet: lucien@eureka.lk.
Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
DAILY NEWS
MORE REBEL BODIES RECOVERED FROM BATTICALOA FIGHTING

Security sources said that intercepted Liberation Tigers of Tamil Eelam (LTTE) transmissions indicated that the number of rebels who died in Monday's fighting in eastern Batticaloa district had risen to 60. Troops have so far recovered 42 bodies. One soldier was killed in the confrontation.
VIRAKESARI
INDIA UNHAPPY OVER KILLING OF ITS FISHERMEN

The Deputy High Commissioner of India in Sri Lanka met Foreign Minister Lakshman Kadirgamar on Tuesday and conveyed his governmenet's unhappiness over the killing of Indian fishermen by the Sri Lankan navy.
The government of the southern Indian state of Tamil Nadu had complained to New Delhi the fishermen were attacked within Indian waters.
THINAKARAN
SRI LANKA PARLIAMENT TO RETAIN ORIGINAL STRENGTH

The earlier proposal of the government to reduce the number of MPs under the draft onstitution has now been reversed and the existing number of 225 MPs will be retained. Of these, 125 will be elected on an electoral basis and 100 on proportional Basis.
The changed proposal was presented by the Minister of Constitutional Affairs Prof. G. L. Peiris at the Parliamentary Select Committee meeting on constitutional reforms held on Tuesday.
DINAMINA
SUPREME COURT RESERVES ORDER IN COORAY CASE

The Supreme Court ON Tuesday reserved its order on the fundamental rights application filed on behalf of Sirisena Cooray, former general secretary of the main opposition United National Party and cabinet minister, challenging his arrest and detention under the Emergency Regulations.
AMNESTY FOR ARMY DESERTERS EXTENDED

The general amnesty for army deserters to return to their posts by July 21 has been further extended till July 26. This was due to numerous requests by parents to grant more time since many of the deserters were unable to meet the earlier deadline due to domestic problems, the defence ministry said.
DIVAINA
SAARC TOURISM MINISTERS MEETING IN SEPTEMBER

A conference of tourism ministers of South Asian Association of Regional cooperation (SARC) will be held on September 23 in Colombo. The conference will be chaired by the Sri Lankan President Chandrika Bandaranaike Kumaratunge. The Sri Lankan delegation will be led by Tourism Minister Dharmasiri Senanayake.

It is expected that discussions will centre around accepting each other's currency within the SAARC region, clearing visa problems when crossing borders and the possibility of having a common visa to all SAARC countries.
